# ASCEND Frontend — rules for agents

**`CLAUDE.md` is the authority** on architecture, the locked stack, scope and
how to talk to the founder. Read it first. This file is the short, mechanical
version: what will fail the build, and what to do instead.

## Run this before you claim to be done

```
npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build
```

`typecheck` and `build` both run `scripts/check-architecture.mjs` first. It is
not advisory — it exits non-zero and stops the build.

## Where a file goes

```
app/         routes only: fetch, map to props, compose. No business logic.
features/    one folder per domain. The unit of ownership.
components/  shared presentational code: ui/, layout/, auth/. No domain logic.
lib/         plumbing with no domain knowledge: api client, supabase, helpers.
```

Imports run one way only, and the guard enforces it:

```
app/  ──▶  features/  ──▶  components/  ──▶  lib/
```

`lib/` importing a feature is a build failure. So is `components/` importing
one. If a shared component needs feature data, either the data is plumbing and
belongs in `lib/`, or the component is not shared and belongs in the feature.

## The feature rule

`features/<name>/index.ts` is the **only** way in. From outside the feature:

```ts
import { ResumeBuilder } from "@/features/resume";        // yes
import { ResumeBuilder } from "@/features/resume/resume-builder";  // build fails
```

Inside a feature, use relative paths (`./resume-sheet`), never `@/features/<own
name>/...`.

Adding a line to a barrel widens that feature's public contract. Do it
deliberately; do not re-export a file just to make an import compile.

**No cycles between features.** If A needs B and B needs A, the boundary is
wrong — usually a shared type or helper that belongs in `lib/`. `Audience` and
`hub-memory` were moved there for exactly this reason.

CSS modules are the one exception: `@/features/x/y.module.css` may be imported
directly, because a barrel cannot usefully re-export CSS.

## File size is a ratchet

800 lines is the ceiling for anything new. Five files were already over it when
the guard was written; each has its size recorded in `SIZE_ALLOWANCE` and **may
only shrink**. Lower the number when you shrink one; delete the line when it
drops under 800. Never raise a number, and never add a new entry — split the
file instead.

## Things that have actually gone wrong here

- **Sync-conflict copies.** This repo lives under `~/Documents`, which iCloud
  syncs; it periodically leaves `admin-console 2.tsx` beside the real file.
  `npm run clean:conflicts` removes them and runs automatically before
  typecheck and build. Never edit or import a ` 2.` file.
- **`"use client"` must be the first line.** Adding an import above it is a
  Turbopack build error, not a type error, so typecheck will not catch it.
- **Components named after DOM globals** (`Text`, `Option`, `Image`) resolve to
  the global instead of erroring when the import is missing. The symptom is
  `TS2786: 'Text' cannot be used as a JSX component`, not "cannot find name".
- **Dead code accumulates invisibly.** 71 preview routes and 32 unreferenced
  components shipped to production for months. If you build a throwaway page to
  look at something, delete it in the same session.
- **Behavioural metrics are never shown to users.** Dwell time, return counts
  and click counts may rank and order things. They must never appear in copy.
  `tests/unit/discovery-direction-card.test.tsx` guards this.

## Never

- Scoring, readiness or business logic in this repo — it belongs in
  `ascend-backend`.
- Direct database access, the Supabase service-role key, or AI SDK calls here.
- Fabricated numbers, invented user counts, ratings or "trusted by" claims.
- New dependencies without asking. The stack is locked (see `CLAUDE.md`).
- `git commit` or `git push` unless the founder explicitly asks. Pushing
  deploys.
